faq.title: Frequently asked questions about the Northern Lights
faq.intro: Everything you need to know to chase the Northern Lights — from Kp values to what to wear at -25 °C.
faq.a.about1: The name RepoTracker comes from a Finnish belief that the Northern Lights are created when a magical fox, "Repo", strikes the snow with its tail, sending sparks into the sky.
faq.a.about2: Who is behind this project? RepoTracker is a solo project, designed and maintained by a single Northern Lights enthusiast. From coding the maps to tracking solar data — everything you see here is the result of one person's passion for the Northern Lights.
faq.a.about3: Because this is a one-person project, your feedback and support mean the world. Every coffee donated helps cover server costs and API fees that keep the real-time data running for everyone.
faq.q.when: When is the best time to see the Northern Lights?
faq.a.when: The Northern Lights are best seen on dark, clear nights in autumn and spring. The best time is usually between 9 p.m. and 2 a.m. In northern Finland, a Kp index of 3–4 is enough; in the south you usually need Kp 5–6 or higher.
faq.q.values: What do the values on the map mean?
faq.a.values: The Kp index describes geomagnetic activity. The higher the value, the more likely Northern Lights are visible:
faq.q.clouds: How does cloud cover affect visibility?
faq.a.clouds: Clouds block the Northern Lights completely. Always check the cloud cover before heading out — a clear sky is essential.
faq.q.dark: Do I need a dark place?
faq.a.dark1: Yes. Light pollution in cities reduces visibility significantly. Move away from street lights and choose an open area with a clear view of the northern horizon.
faq.a.dark2: It is still possible to see Northern Lights in towns like Rovaniemi — just step into a slightly darker spot and you have a good chance when the forecast is favorable.
faq.a.dark3: Tip: sometimes a phone camera picks up the Northern Lights before your eyes do.
faq.q.south: Can the Northern Lights be seen in southern Finland?
faq.a.south: Yes, but less frequently. A high Kp index (≥ 5–6) and clear skies are required.
faq.q.know: How do I know when the Northern Lights will appear?
faq.a.know: Use real-time tools like RepoTracker for live forecasts. You can also follow data from NOAA SWPC and the Finnish Meteorological Institute.
faq.q.bz: What are solar wind and IMF Bz?
faq.a.bz: The solar wind is a stream of charged particles from the Sun that delivers energy to Earth's magnetic field. The IMF Bz value indicates the orientation of the interplanetary magnetic field — a strong negative Bz greatly increases the chances of seeing the Northern Lights.
faq.q.gear: What should you keep in mind when going hunting for the Northern Lights?
faq.a.gear1: Dress warmly — one thick coat is not the best option. Several thin layers under a proper winter coat keep you warmer and give flexibility.
faq.a.gear2: Wear warm shoes and gloves, and bring extra clothes if you plan to be outside for a long time.
faq.a.gear3: If you are traveling by rental car, stay on plowed public roads. Do not drive on poorly maintained or unplowed forest roads — you can get stuck in the snow and help may take a long time to arrive in winter.
faq.a.gear4: If you head out on your own, respect private yards, military areas and any place where you are unsure whether entry is allowed.
faq.a.gear5: Tip: be careful where you stop the car. Bus stops are ideal. Avoid stopping on the road to prevent dangerous situations.
faq.a.tips1: Useful safety guidance for visitors to Lapland is available as a PDF from the Finnish rescue services.
faq.a.tips2: A few good Northern Lights-watching spots near Rovaniemi: Ounasvaara, Olkkajärvi parking lot near Apukka Resort, and Arktikum Park.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: How RepoTracker handles your data, cookies and analytics.
privacy.a.about1: RepoTracker is a real-time monitoring tool for Northern Lights enthusiasts. Our mission is to provide accurate, easy-to-read space weather data to help users predict and see the Northern Lights.
privacy.a.about2: RepoTracker is committed to protecting your privacy. This policy explains how we handle information and use cookies when you visit our website.
privacy.a.data1: We do not collect personal information simply based on your browsing of the site. We collect personal information (such as your email address) only when you contact us via a form or purchase a Premium service. Note, however, that the site loads maps, images and other content from third-party services which see your IP address — see the section "Third-party services and your IP address". We may also use analytics services to understand how visitors use the site. These services use cookies to collect anonymous data, such as:
privacy.a.data3: Time spent on the site and pages visited.
privacy.a.data5: This data is used solely to improve the user experience and monitor the technical performance of the service.
privacy.a.location1: The site uses your location only when you grant permission in your browser, and only for the feature you are using: showing the forecast for your location, reporting a sighting, or targeting alerts. Your location is never tracked in the background.
privacy.a.location2: When you report a sighting, the location is stored at roughly one kilometre accuracy and appears on the map for two hours. Your exact position is not stored.
privacy.a.location3: To measure forecast accuracy we additionally store an area rounded to roughly 50 kilometres, the time rounded to the hour, the conditions at that moment, and whether the lights were visible.
privacy.a.location4: For alerts, the location you choose is stored to two decimal places so we can notify you when conditions improve.
privacy.a.location5: Sighting records contain no name, email address or user account. A salted hash is used to detect spam reports, and the salt changes each season — the same device cannot be linked across seasons.
privacy.a.location6: These observations are used only to assess and improve forecast accuracy. They are never sold or shared with third parties.
privacy.a.ads1: Third-party vendors, including Google, may use cookies to serve ads based on a user's prior visits to this website or other websites.
privacy.a.ads2: These advertising cookies enable Google and its partners to serve ads based on visits to this and other sites on the Internet.
privacy.a.ads3: You can opt out of personalized advertising through Google's Ads Settings.
privacy.a.cookies: You can disable cookies through your browser settings at any time.

privacy.a.terms2: Use of Service. RepoTracker is a tool for tracking Northern Lights-related space weather data. You agree to use it only for lawful purposes and in a manner that does not infringe the rights of others.
